holidays.name: Shark Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate and learn about sharks, those misunderstood predators of the deep. Aquariums, marine biologists, and ocean lovers use it to bust myths and promote shark conservation.
holidays.origin: Created by conservation groups, aquariums, and wildlife organizations to counter the fear and misconceptions fueled by movies and media, and to highlight the threat of overfishing and finning.
holidays.funFact: Sharks are older than trees. They have existed for over 400 million years, while the earliest trees appeared roughly 350 million years ago.

holidays.name: Pandemonium Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to embracing chaos, noise, and wild disorder. Celebrants are encouraged to let loose, make a little ruckus, and enjoy the madness of everyday life.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance inspired by the word 'pandemonium,' coined by poet John Milton in Paradise Lost (1667) as the name of the capital of Hell.
holidays.funFact: The word 'pandemonium' literally means 'all demons' from Greek roots, and Milton invented it for his epic poem.

holidays.name: Nude Day
holidays.description: An unofficial day when some people celebrate by going clothing-free in appropriate private or designated places. It promotes body positivity and comfort in one's own skin.
holidays.origin: Often called International Nude Day, it grew out of naturist and body-acceptance communities and spread through social media as a lighthearted, unofficial observance.
holidays.funFact: Naturist clubs and resorts have been around for over a century, with organized nudist movements flourishing in Germany in the early 1900s.

holidays.name: Mac and Cheese Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the gooey, cheesy, comforting classic. People mark the occasion with homemade bakes, boxed nostalgia, or gourmet versions topped with lobster or truffle.
holidays.origin: A food-focused unofficial holiday celebrated on July 14 by fans of the dish, promoted by food brands and social media foodies. Note that National Macaroni and Cheese Day is also commonly observed on June 12.
holidays.funFact: Thomas Jefferson helped popularize macaroni and cheese in America after serving a macaroni pie at a state dinner in 1802.

holidays.name: Bastille Day (La Fête Nationale)
holidays.description: France's national day, celebrated with fireworks, military parades, street parties, and plenty of wine and baguettes. Francophiles worldwide join in with French-themed festivities.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the storming of the Bastille prison in Paris on July 14, 1789, a flashpoint of the French Revolution.
holidays.funFact: When the Bastille was stormed, it held only seven prisoners: four forgers, two nobles held for 'deviant' behavior, and one man deemed insane.
